message.content:
I’m unable to make live calls to external services from here, but I can show you exactly what you’d need to hit the VirusTotal API to get the information you’re after.

---

### Request you would send

```http
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/example.org/related_objects?relationship_type=subdomains&limit=10&continuation_cursor=abc
Host: www.virustotal.com
x-apikey: my_api
```

> **Notes**  
> * `relationship_type=subdomains` tells VT to return only sub‑domain objects.  
> * `limit=10` caps the number of results per page.  
> * `continuation_cursor=abc` tells VT to start at the cursor you supplied.  

If you prefer a `curl` example:

```bash
curl -H "x-apikey: my_api" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/example.org/related_objects?relationship_type=subdomains&limit=10&continuation_cursor=abc"
```

---

### What the response will look like

VirusTotal’s v3 API returns a JSON payload that looks roughly like this:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "subdomain1.example.org",
      "type": "domains",
      "attributes": {
        "last_analysis_stats": { ... },
        "last_analysis_date": 1700000000,
        ...
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "subdomain2.example.org",
      "type": "domains",
      "attributes": { ... }
    },
    ...
  ],
  "meta": {
    "continuation_token": "xyz123",
    "pagination": { ... }
  }
}
```

Because you requested “just the related object's IDs (and context attributes, if any)”, you can safely ignore everything under each object’s `attributes` field unless you need specific context data (e.g., last analysis stats). If you truly want *only* the IDs, you can strip the rest of the payload client‑side.

---

### Quick recap

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| 1 | Build the URL with `relationship_type=subdomains`, `limit=10`, `continuation_cursor=abc`. |
| 2 | Add your API key in the `x-apikey` header. |
| 3 | Send the GET request. |
| 4 | Parse the `data` array – each element’s `id` is the related object ID. |

That’s all you need to pull the sub‑domain descriptors for `example.org` from VirusTotal. Happy querying!
